relatedSnapshot.title: Charged twice for the same domain and inbox bundle; one bundle was never delivered and its subscription is still billing
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context: customer-initiated Intercom conversation, opened 2026-09-30, contact Name 1 <email>, workspace "Name 2 Workspace", owner role. Initial message: "I have a billing issue that isn't being sorted. Please escalate to someone asap!" Asked for detail: "I've been billed twice for emails and domains for the last 3 months when that's not what I'm using." Declined the self-serve answer: "No, I still need help." No attachments.

Bucket: overcharged.

Finding: the customer bought the same DFY bundle (1 domain + 3 inboxes) twice about 17 hours apart and was charged for both; only one bundle was ever delivered. Order <uuid> (domain <domain>, created 2026-07-23 14:01Z) was cancelled for "Payment timeout - order automatically cancelled after 30 minutes" with nothing provisioned, but its Autumn subscription and its Stripe charges landed anyway. Order <uuid> (domain <domain>, created 2026-07-24 06:47Z) completed and is the bundle the customer actually uses (3 active connected inboxes). The cancelled order's subscription was never cancelled, so it has kept invoicing every month since.

Exposure (Stripe, smallest currency unit, all succeeded and unrefunded, no credit notes):

* 2026-07-23, 3276 cents ($32.76), charge <stripe-id>, invoice EKGUJ5YE-0017
* 2026-08-23, 1800 cents ($18.00), charge <stripe-id>, invoice EKGUJ5YE-0021

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer report: overbilled for cancelled domains and inboxes on the shared Name 3 billing account
relatedSnapshot.description:
Source: Intercom conversation 215476145402779 (contact <email>), workspace Name 3.

Ask (taxonomy bucket): refund. The customer reports being overbilled for inboxes, asks for a credit back of the appropriate amount, and asks us to cancel what he calls the bugs.

What he reports, verbatim in substance: "I am being overbilled in my workspace for the number of inboxes I am using ... It says I am paying for 11 Domains and 33 inboxes", "when I am in my workspace, it only shows a total of 7 domains and 21 inboxes", "there are only 18 inboxes working in the workspace", "Obviously, I don't want to be charged today and tomorrow for a bunch of inboxes that I'm not even using. I can't figure out where the charges are coming from and how to cancel them." Three screenshots were attached (billing page, workspace summary, email account list); the image-reading lane could not run, so the exact screen behind "11 Domains" is unconfirmed.

Finding: One billing account (<uuid>, native Autumn, no partner) is shared by three workspaces he owns: Name 3, Name 4 and Name 5. Production shows Name 3 holding 7 active domains and 21 inboxes (18 connected + 3 pending since 5 March), while the other two workspaces hold 11 suspended domains and 33 inboxes cancelled at the provider ("Mailbox cancelled by user"), five of those domains with cancelled provider subscriptions and the rest with none. Autumn and Stripe still carry 15 domain seats a year and 33 inbox seats a month on live subscriptions, so $264.00 a month is charged for 33 inbox seats and $270.00 a year for 15 domain seats against 7 working domains and 18 working inboxes in the whole account. Charged seats for dead resources have never been removed and nothing has been refunded; the in-app cancellation cannot reconcile a shared billing account across workspaces.

Exposure: $264.00/month for 33 inbox seats and $270.00/year for 15 domain seats; the audit snapshot of 2026-09-27 already marks the suspended-domain findings "overcharged" and records billed coverage beyond active holdings.

Discretion: needs-human. No prior approval or promise exists; the deciding amount and the mapping of each charged subscription to the workspace it covers need a person.

Proposed human action (a proposal, never a promise): reconcile the live add-on subscriptions on billing account <uuid> against the resources that are still live, cancel or reduce the seats that cover the suspended/cancelled resources, and refund the charges taken after those resources stopped working, then tell the customer which subscriptions were stopped and what was credited.

relatedSnapshot.title: Billing card shows CMR-ended domains as Active while they are still billed
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

The CMR domain audit marks a domain `overcharged` when CMR has ended it but Autumn/Whop billing still renews (e.g. a domain cancelled in CMR on Sep 25 with inbox billing still renewing Oct 25).

The **customer** billing card had no case for `overcharged`, so those domains showed:

* no billing badge
* inboxes labelled **Active**
* a **"Payment due"** countdown

So a customer paying for a domain that no longer exists saw the opposite of the truth, with no signal that anything was wrong. The admin side has flagged this since ENG-14258; the customer side never did.

## Solution

* `DomainBillingBadge`: `overcharged` renders **"Ended <date> · Still billed"** (warning) with a tooltip telling the customer to cancel to stop billing.
* New `isOverchargedDomainBilling` and `isEndedDomainBilling` helpers.
* `EmailAccountsDomainsCard`: for ended domains (inactive or overcharged), inboxes show **"Ended"** and the payment-due column is hidden.
* The **Cancel button stays** for overcharged domains — `cancelManagedDomainInProvider` already treats CMR "already cancelled / not found" as success, so cancelling proceeds to cancel the billing. This is the customer's self-serve fix.

## Regression guard

Adds a test that **every** audit payment state renders a badge except the internal `unlinked` and `error`, so a newly added state cannot silently render nothing again — which is exactly how this bug arose when `overcharged` was introduced.

## Testing

* `bunx vitest run tests/components/billing/domain-billing-badge.test.tsx` — 11 passed.
* Biome, tsc on changed files, `check-v2 --changed` clean.

## Coordination note

Acquisity/Acquisity#6642 (ENG-14340) also edits `email-accounts-domains-card.tsx` and is still open. The two are logically consistent — ENG-14340 hides Cancel for `cmr_inactive` (nothing left to cancel), this one deliberately keeps it for `overcharged` (billing is still running, so cancelling is the fix) — but they will likely conflict in that file. Worth landing them in a deliberate order.

## Notes

3 files, +55/-4. Part of the CMR domain audit series.

relatedSnapshot.title: Flag inactive CMR domains that are still billed as overcharged
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Since Acquisity/Acquisity#6595, the CMR Domain Subscription Audit records domains that are INACTIVE or EXPIRED at ColdMailReseller as `cmr_inactive`. It doesn't check whether the customer is still being billed for them, so a customer paying for a domain that no longer exists at CMR looks identical to one who stopped paying.

There is also a quieter bug: a dedicated billing subscription for an inactive domain went into the group's shared pool and could count as coverage for an active domain, hiding an unpaid active domain.

## Root cause

Classification only matched billing subscriptions against active domains. Anything attached to an inactive domain was treated as unmatched pool coverage, and inactive domains were never compared against billing.

## Solution

* Match subscriptions against every domain in a billing group. A subscription dedicated to an inactive domain stays with that domain and no longer covers active ones.
* New payment state `overcharged` for an inactive domain that is still billed. It applies when either:
  * its dedicated domain/inbox subscription is active and not scheduled to end, or
  * pooled (unmatched) billing covers more domains/inboxes than the group's active domains need. Surplus is assigned to inactive domains alphabetically: one domain each, inboxes up to each domain's inbox count. If the surplus comes from the billing feature ledger, the note says it may include comped grants.
* Billing already scheduled to end is not flagged. The domain stays `cmr_inactive` with "billing ends YYYY-MM-DD" in the note.
* Groups where every domain is inactive now get a billing lookup (Acquisity/Acquisity#6595 skipped this).
* `overcharged` has severity 3, is included in "Action needed", the run summary's actionable list, and a new "Overcharged" tab with an amber badge. It is not a CMR-cancellable state (the domain is already dead at CMR; the fix is on the billing side) but it can be dismissed.
* Migration widens `cmr_domain_audit_finding_payment_state_check` with `overcharged` using `NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE`, following Acquisity/Acquisity#6595.

## Impact

* **User:** none directly. Admins can now find customers paying for dead domains and refund/cancel that billing.
* **Business:** catches overbilling before it becomes a support ticket or chargeback, and stops inactive domains hiding underpayment on active ones.

## Testing

7 new unit tests covering: a dedicated subscription still billing an inactive domain; an inactive domain's subscription no longer covering an active one; surplus from pooled domain billing; surplus from pooled inbox billing split across inactive domains; billing scheduled to end; surplus from the billing feature ledger; and groups where every domain is inactive. Audit, admin, renewal, cancel suites and the snapshot DB test (which applies the migration) also pass.

## Notes

* Expect some active domains to move from `paid` to `unpaid`/`underpaid` on the first run.
* When overcharge comes from pooled billing, which inactive domain carries it is arbitrary; the group total is correct.
* Not covered: billing for domains that have disappeared from CMR entirely (no finding row to attach it to).
* Rollback: revert the PR. The widened constraint is harmless if left in place.

Follows Acquisity/Acquisity#6595.

relatedSnapshot.title: Name 6 — billed $1,436 for 18 inboxes never created, $144/month still renewing
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Bounded context: customer opened with "cancel all subscriptions and billing", then reported he has never had any inboxes or domains but is being charged for both; cancelling his legacy plan lowered the next bill by only $1; Manage Billing shows no subscription list to cancel; the remaining line item is labelled "inbox - inboxes - 18 x 8". He was escalated to a human and has had no answer.

Claim: 18 inboxes were charged at $8/month from 2025-12-03 to date, and $107.77 for 6 pre-warmed domains, but the workspace holds no domains or inboxes, has no outreach account connected, and the purchase record shows 0 of 18 mailbox creations succeeded, so the customer paid for a year of inbox capacity that never existed and has no self-serve control to stop the recurring charge.

Ask bucket: overcharged (money).

Verified money (Stripe, <stripe-id>): $1,554.08 USD collected across 12 paid invoices; nothing refunded; no credit notes; balance 0; no dispute. Of that, $1,436.31 is the 18-inbox charge (first month prorated $140.31 plus nine months at $144.00) and $107.77 is the domain year; $10.00 is the Legacy plan.

Forward exposure: $145.00 due 2026-10-02 and $108.00 due 2026-12-02, then $145.00 monthly, with no in-product cancellation path.

Why there is no cancel path (current code): the Billing page card renders from org mail_domain rows only and shows "No managed domains" when there are none, offering no Cancel control; cancellation runs through cancelManagedDomains, which returns "Domain is not managed by this workspace" when no mail_domain row exists. Cancelling the named plan product cancels only that product, which is the $1 reduction the customer saw. Repository HEAD read: f0228bab1e57b287a17a66e2e042abc3de8191dd.

Discretion: needs-human. All three systems of record agree the add-ons are live and paid, so this is not a sync fault; the divergence is between what was paid for and what exists in the workspace. No prior approval or promise exists in the conversation or the request, so the amount decision is a person's.

Proposed human action (proposal, not a promise):

1. Cancel the live Inbox add-on ($8 x 18) and the Domain add-on on billing account 7de4ed09.../Stripe subscription <stripe-id> before the 2026-10-02 renewal, so the October and December charges cannot land.
2. Decide the refund: $1,436.31 for inbox capacity never created plus an amount for the domain year the customer never had visible, out of $1,554.08 collected. No refund or credit has been issued.
3. Tell the customer, because he has had no answer since Fin AI escalated him on 2026-09-29.

Unverified on this ticket: the customer's purchase intent at signup; whether the December 2025 order flow code matches today's HEAD, so no failing function is attributed; the provider-side cancellation record for these six domains (the cancellation log table starts 2026-08-01 and holds no row for them).

relatedSnapshot.description:
## Ask (taxonomy bucket: refund)

Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Bounded context: the customer reports he "spent £250 on domains" that never appeared, says a later attempt to buy 10 more domains "didn't work", asks twice for a refund of "these domain purchases that didn't show", and wants his workspace grown from 63 to 126 inboxes (he says 30 extra inboxes he bought also did not arrive). Conversation opened 2026-09-22 07:34 UTC and is still open.

## Finding

Two pre-warmed domain + inbox orders in the "Name 9" workspace (organization <uuid>) were charged and then cancelled before provisioning started, so no domains and no inboxes were created and the value returned to the account as a balance credit instead of to the card:

* 14 Sep 2026 16:05 UTC: $336.00 charged (8 domains + 24 inboxes). Order cancelled 16:49 UTC, domains_provisioned 0, inboxes_provisioned 0.
* 22 Sep 2026 07:40 UTC: $357.28 charged (10 domains + 30 inboxes, $62.72 of existing credit applied). Order cancelled 07:45 UTC, domains_provisioned 0, inboxes_provisioned 0.

A third attempt on 14 Sep 17:04 was fully covered by the credit from the first cancellation. The 14 Sep charge was never refunded to the card; $272.00 of the resulting credit later paid two invoices (16 and 18 Sep) for inboxes and domains the customer still has.

No new sending accounts exist in his Company One workspace since 7 May 2026, so nothing was delivered by any of the September orders.

## Exposure

* $693.84 charged to the card across the window (336.00 + 0.56 + 357.28).
* $420.00 currently sits as a customer-balance credit on the billing account.
* $272.00 of that credit was consumed by two later invoices for services the customer keeps.

## Proposed human action (a proposal, not a promise)

Refund the $420.00 balance credit to the card originally charged. Alternative if the customer prefers to keep buying: apply the credit to a replacement pre-warmed domain + inbox order that actually provisions. Both need a finance decision; no money has been moved.

Related product context only, no engineering work requested here: the charge-then-cancel shape is covered by existing engineering work (ENG-13358 master, ENG-14067).

relatedSnapshot.title: ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error: reconnect sends mailboxId=undefined ("Mailbox not found")
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Pre-warmed mailboxes provisioned through ColdMailReseller get stuck in an Error state and cannot send, because no reconnect path resolves a mailbox id the provider will accept.

## Problem

When a ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inbox disconnects or needs reconnecting, the account-error reconnect flow fires with `mailboxId: providerId ?? undefined`. These inboxes have `mail_inbox.provider_id = NULL`, so the provider receives `mailboxId=undefined` and the OAuth connect returns "Mailbox not found", leaving the inbox permanently in Error.

## Root cause

`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-account-error-reconnect.ts` invokes `processConnectOAuth` with `mailboxId: inboxLookup.providerId ?? undefined`. `processConnectOAuth` (`process-connect-oauth.ts`, `connect-mailbox-oauth` step) forwards that `mailboxId` to ColdMailReseller `POST /mailboxes/oauth` via `apps/web/lib/mail/providers/coldmailreseller/client.ts#connectMailboxOAuth`, which rejects it with "Mailbox not found". The inboxes have `mail_inbox.provider_id = NULL`, so the id is never resolved. The reconcile cron (`reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`) already looks up the mailbox from ColdMailReseller and passes `mailbox.id` correctly, so the resolution pattern exists.

The failing invariant is one gap across every entry point: no reconnect path resolves the mailbox id from ColdMailReseller before calling the provider. The webhook path forwards the stored `mail_inbox.provider_id`; the customer Reconnect action (`email-accounts.ts`, `triggerOAuthReconnect`) and the admin reconnect (`admin-domain-orders.ts`) both send `mailboxId: undefined`; `processConnectOAuth` never re-resolves. An inbox carrying a named but no-longer-valid id fails identically to one with a NULL id, which is why both counts below sit in this one class.

## Blast radius

5,762 inboxes across 444 organizations carry a `connection_error` containing "Mailbox not found" (query: `SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT organization_id) FROM mail_inbox WHERE connection_error ILIKE '%Mailbox not found%'`, counted 2026-09-24: 5,762 inboxes / 444 organizations, and 7,071 reconnect sessions across 461 organizations failed the same way in the 30 days to 2026-09-24; was 5,763 / 445 on 2026-09-23, 5,660 / 439 on 2026-09-22, 4,364 / 323 on 2026-09-10 and 294 / 39 on 2026-08-28). None of the 5,762 is connected now. 2,391 of them carry the exact `mailboxId=undefined` signature (and all of those have `provider_id IS NULL`); the larger 3,371 carry a named mailbox id and fail the same way. Named-id rows arrive in platform waves (2026-09-04 to 09-06 roughly 2,118 rows across 95+ organizations; 2026-09-19 to 09-20 roughly 1,148 rows across 103 organizations), so the shape is systematic rather than org-specific. A further 2,872 connected pre-warmed inboxes across 228 organizations sit at `provider_id IS NULL` and would fail the same way on their next reconnect.

## Proposed fix

Resolve the provider mailbox id before reconnecting: look up the mailbox from ColdMailReseller (as the reconcile cron already does) instead of passing `provider_id` or `undefined`, and backfill `provider_id` for the affected inboxes so they reconnect successfully.

## Done when

* No reconnect path hands ColdMailReseller an unresolved id: the webhook path stops forwarding the stored `provider_id` unresolved, the customer Reconnect and admin reconnect stop sending `undefined`, and both shapes (NULL `provider_id` and stale named id) reconnect successfully.
* The stuck inboxes are recovered or re-provisioned and resume sending.
* Provider accounts with no local `mail_inbox` row are covered too: Reconnect refuses them outright (`email-accounts.ts#triggerOAuthReconnect` throws PRECONDITION_FAILED "Only managed inboxes can be reconnected.") while their inbox entitlements are still consumed, so the backfill and re-provision step must create or link the missing rows, not only repair a NULL or stale `provider_id`.

## Reports

* ENG-13156
* ENG-13255
* ENG-13511
* ENG-14104
* ENG-14131
* ENG-14197 Customer report: all 15 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error; Reconnect returns Mailbox not found; campaigns cannot send
* ENG-14201 Customer report: 15 of 36 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error; Reconnect returns Mailbox not found and never clears the inbox
